## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling even with list-based intermediates and irregular append.

## Cache saturation
All measured N (10000–10000000) exceed the L1d spill at N≈910, so the L1d regime is unseen. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from 8.549 ns/p (N=10000, below L2 spill at N≈58254) to 7.741 (N=100000, above it) — overhead amortization, not a cache knee, since the L2→DRAM transition shows no rise. Cost stays FLAT at 7.806 and 7.555 for N=1M and 10M. At q=0.1, cost is FLAT at ~9.28–9.29 from 10K to 100K, then RISES to 10.447 at 1M — a mild DRAM-latency effect, not an L2-spill knee. At q=0.25 and q=0.5, cost is FLAT across all N (11.8 and 15.7 ns/p respectively): death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape. No cache-spill knee appears at any death rate.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.53 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 31.9% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth FALLS monotonically with death rate: 7.76 GB/s (26%) at q=0.1, 6.11 GB/s (20%) at q=0.25, 4.56 GB/s (15%) at q=0.5. The algo is never bandwidth-bound; at q=0.01 it is compute-bound (64.8% compute, 31.6% backend stall) and transitions to branch-overhead-bound by q=0.5 (46.5% compute, 35.0% branch_flush). The transition is driven entirely by death rate, not by N.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized the per-particle physics update component-wise, not across particles: `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` process 4 position floats, `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` process 2 velocity floats, with `ext.16b` and `mov.s v18[3]` rearranging components within one particle's 72-byte record. A gather appears — `ld1.s {v17}[1], [x10]` loads a single element into a vector lane — reflecting the list intermediate's irregular access. The deposit phase is entirely scalar byte operations: 19 `strb` and 12 `ldrb` with `csel` saturation clamps. These byte-granular scatter stores cap bandwidth at 32% of ceiling; the component-wise vectorization of the update cannot compensate for the non-streaming scatter.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 9.53 GB/s = 31.9% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling (q=0.01, N=10M), and falls to 4.56 GB/s = 15% at q=0.5. The list intermediate's gather (`ld1.s`) and the scatter's 19 `strb` byte stores prevent streaming, while branch_flush rises to 35% at high death rates. Auto-vectorization of the per-particle update is present but cannot approach the streaming ceiling.
